field: Registered Nursing, Nursing Administration, Nursing Research and Clinical Nursing

leads_to.evidence: Graduates must pass the NCLEX-RN and get a state license before they can work as registered nurses. Most go straight into staff RN jobs.

nearby_pair.evidence: Miami Dade College's BSN is an RN-to-BSN program that requires a nursing associate degree and a Florida RN license, so its graduates are already working nurses. Florida National University runs a pre-licensure BSN with an entrance exam.

school_matters.evidence: Every new RN must pass the same NCLEX-RN licensing exam, so the license sets a common entry floor. Pay is about the same whether a school admits under a tenth or most applicants, and it follows region and hospital more than the school's name.

who_is_counted.evidence: The largest programs pay above the major's median, and half of them are pooled or online-only. That pattern fits RN-to-BSN completion programs, which admit only nurses who already hold an RN license and an associate degree. I did not check which programs are the largest.

programs.evidence: Mercy University runs an online RN to B.S. completion program for registered nurses who already hold an associate degree or diploma in nursing. Those already-employed nurses are likely counted together with its traditional BSN graduates.
Pacific College's BSN is an RN-to-BSN completion program taught by distance education, so its graduates are already licensed, working nurses.
Sonoma State is in Northern California, which pays registered nurses more than anywhere else in the country. It also runs an RN-to-BSN track for nurses who are already licensed.
Registered nurses in Puerto Rico earn far less than nurses on the mainland, so all of the island's nursing programs report low pay.
